title: Token-window precision sentinel and prefill consolidator for mixed INT8/FP8 kernel selection
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem statement: Dequant overhead and mixed-precision transitions during prefill and decode increase tail latency on multi-tenant inference hosts. Current kernel arbitration heuristics pick an INT8 fastpath or an FP8 fallback per-layer, but they react per-request without global view of the token window and headwise memory pressure. This leads to repeated dequant/requant cycles, KV cache format churn, and suboptimal scheduling for streaming workloads.

Goal: Implement a lightweight token-window precision sentinel plus a prefill consolidator that: (1) collects short-window telemetry across microbatches to decide a stable precision plan for the next N tokens; (2) groups contiguous prefill work across heads to avoid per-layer format toggles; and (3) exposes a tunable pressure threshold to prefer FP8 on high headwise-activation variance. The sentinel should be cheap (few KB of state per request) and respect existing latency SLOs.

Key deliverables: 
- Token-window precision sentinel: runtime component that samples latency, KV cache growth, and headwise activation variance across the last M tokens and outputs a precision recommendation (INT8|FP8|mix) and recommended kernel bundle.
- Prefill consolidator: scheduler stage that merges adjacent prefill slices when the sentinel indicates stable precision, emitting batched kernel calls to fused kernels that avoid dequant bounce.
- Headwise staging policy: when variance across attention heads exceeds threshold, prefer per-head mixed execution to reduce end-to-end dequant cost.
- Telemetry and metrics: add sentinel decisions to token-level traces and a dashboard for precision flip rate, dequant penalty, and tail latency impact.

Design notes / trade-offs considered: 
- Aggressiveness vs safety: Conservative approach reduces precision flips but may miss short bursts where INT8 is safe. We will default to a one-token lookahead conservative policy, tunable by rollout.
- Statefulness vs statelessness: Keeping per-request sentinel state for N tokens increases memory charge for long-lived streaming requests. We bound sentinel state at 64 tokens and expose eviction heuristics.
- Complexity of headwise mixed execution: Introducing headwise staging increases kernel variety. To mitigate combinatorial explosion, we only allow headwise staging when sentinel detects >1.5x head variance and fall back to whole-layer decision otherwise.
- Compatibility: Integrate with existing kernel catalog and runtime kernel selector. Sentinel outputs map to existing kernel bundle IDs to avoid new kernel proliferation.

Acceptance criteria: 
- 5-10% reduction in 99th percentile latency on streaming chat benchmark with quantized models (gpt-style), measured under production-like load.
- Reduction in per-request dequant/requant toggles by >40% in A/B test.
- No regression in median latency or token throughput.

Implementation plan (high level): 
1) Prototype sentinel collector in user-space runtime shim (non-blocking) and add token-level tracing hooks (2w).
2) Implement prefill consolidator in the scheduler with safe guardrails (3w).
3) Add headwise staging gates and map to existing fused kernels (2w).
4) Add telemetry and config toggles in Redwood Console (1w).
5) Canary rollout to dedicated cluster with AB measurement (2w).

Links and artifacts: 
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.company/confluence/runtime-precision/token-window-sentinel 
- Design sketch (draw.io): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1-token-window-dwg 
- Benchmark plan (sheets): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-quant-bench-plan 

Notes on integration: 
- The sentinel must be consulted by the kernel arbitrator prior to kernel selection for the first prefill microbatch and after any KV cache format transition.
- Prefill consolidator should prefer fused-kernel bundles (existing kernel ids) to minimize kernel registration churn.
- Telemetry tagging: include sentinel_decision and sentinel_confidence in token traces.

Risks and mitigation: 
- Incorrect sentinel thresholds could cause precision drift and quality regressions. Mitigate with canary and automated quality-eval harness per rollout.
- Memory overhead for sentinel state: cap token-window and evict oldest entries; provide a per-tenant knob.

Next steps (this ticket): 
- Build prototype collector and add initial telemetry hooks (Diego).
- Draft unit tests for consolidator semantics (Asha).
- Review kernel bundle mapping with Kernel Team (RFC scheduled).
comments: 2025-02-11 - Diego Ruiz: Kickoff done, prototype sketch attached. Will start with trace-based collector. Added initial perf harness to staging.
2025-02-18 - Asha Menon: Implemented sentinel proto that samples headwise l2 variance and token latency. Observed noisy signals at token granularity; smoothing window of 8 tokens reduced flips.
2025-02-22 - Kernel Team (via PR #1147): Reviewed bundle mappings. Agreed to reuse bundle-id k-bundle-v3 for fused prefill when sentinel recommends INT8 stable window.

2025-02-27 - Diego Ruiz: Prefill consolidator basic merge implemented. Integration test added; discovered an edge-case where KV cache layout mismatch causes a kernel assert — added safety check that forces format normalization before merged prefill if layouts differ.
2025-03-02 - PM Review (Sofia Patel): Great progress. Please add a feature flag and runtime knob for headwise staging; product wants safe default off for first canary.
2025-03-03 - Diego Ruiz: Added feature flag runtime.precision.token_window.enabled=false by default. Will enable in canary cluster next week.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus on the sentinel's sampling cost and the prefill consolidator's safety checks. Kernel Team should verify bundle mapping to avoid new kernel registries. Perf team: validate 99p latency on streaming chat under 80% utilization.
